# e-ORP CSV File Reference

***This document was generated by Claude AI, and may contain errors.***

This document describes the CSV files produced by the e-ORP (Optimal
Retirement Planner) application. e-ORP uses a Mixed Integer Non-Linear
Programming (MINLP) solver (SCIP via PySCIPopt) to optimise
tax-efficient withdrawal and Roth conversion strategies across a
retirement planning horizon.

**Important note on units: all monetary values in the CSV files are
expressed in thousands of dollars (\$000s). For example, a value of 50.0
represents \$50,000.**

Row 0 in every CSV file is the base year (the year before planning
begins). It holds initial account balances and model configuration
parameters. Rows 1 through N are the plan years.

Some row-0 cells serve double duty as "squirrelled" metadata storage
(configuration settings that are not naturally associated with any
single year). These are documented in the Row 0 Metadata section below.

# 1. explore.csv (Main Projection Output)

File name configured by the user in the 'With output to:' field; default
data/\_explore.csv. This is the primary output file written after a
normal projection run. It contains the full planning data dictionary
(dd) for every year from the base year (row 0) through the end of the
planning horizon.

Index column: year (calendar year). The file is written by display_dd()
via dfr.to_csv(fname).

## 1.1 Identity Columns

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                          |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| year       | Calendar year (also the row index). Row 0 is the base year; rows 1..N are plan years.    |
| e          | Age of the primary person (Person) at the end of this year.                              |
| j          | Age of the spouse at the end of this year. 0 if no spouse or not Married Filing Jointly. |

## 1.2 Account Balances (end of year, $000s)

These represent the total value of each account at year-end after all
transactions for that year.

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                                                                                               |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| afterTax   | Total value of the After-Tax (taxable brokerage) account.                                                                                                     |
| e_Taxd     | Person's Tax-Deferred account balance (Traditional IRA, 401(k), etc.).                                                                                        |
| j_Taxd     | Spouse's Tax-Deferred account balance.                                                                                                                        |
| e_Roth     | Person's Roth IRA / Roth 401(k) balance.                                                                                                                      |
| j_Roth     | Spouse's Roth IRA / Roth 401(k) balance.                                                                                                                      |
| net_pretax | Total of all accounts at nominal (pre-tax) value: afterTax + e_Taxd + j_Taxd + e_Roth + j_Roth. Used as the Plan Surplus (FTAB) metric.                       |
| net_postax | Estimated post-tax value of all accounts, discounting tax-deferred balances by the marginal income tax rate and after-tax balances by the capital gains rate. |

## 1.3 After-Tax Account Sub-components ($000s)

The after-tax (taxable brokerage) account is decomposed into three asset
sub-classes to allow the optimizer to track unrealised gains and basis
accurately.

| **Column**   | **Description**                                                                                  |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| aTax\_\_cash | Cash (or money market) portion of the after-tax account.                                         |
| aTax_bonds   | Bond portion of the after-tax account.                                                           |
| aTax_basis   | Aggregate cost basis of the stock portion of the after-tax account.                              |
| aTax_unrlz   | Net unrealised gain (positive) or loss (negative) in the stock portion of the after-tax account. |

## 1.4 Withdrawals from Accounts ($000s)

These columns record how much was taken out of each account during the
year.

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                                                    |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| e_RMD      | Person's Required Minimum Distribution from their Tax-Deferred account. Mandatory once the person reaches age 73.  |
| j_RMD      | Spouse's Required Minimum Distribution from their Tax-Deferred account.                                            |
| from_eTaxd | Discretionary withdrawal from the Person's Tax-Deferred account (above and beyond the RMD).                        |
| from_jTaxd | Discretionary withdrawal from the Spouse's Tax-Deferred account.                                                   |
| from_aTax  | Net withdrawal from the After-Tax account (positive = money taken out for spending).                               |
| to_aTax    | Amount deposited into the After-Tax account (e.g. excess income redirected to savings). Positive = money going in. |
| from_eRoth | Withdrawal from the Person's Roth account.                                                                         |
| from_jRoth | Withdrawal from the Spouse's Roth account.                                                                         |

## 1.5 After-Tax Account Transaction Detail ($000s)

These columns decompose the flows into and out of the after-tax account
into cash, bond, and stock-basis sub-components. fm\_ prefix = 'from'
(outflow); to\_ prefix = 'to' (inflow).

| **Column**      | **Description**                                                         |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| fm_aTax\_\_cash | Cash withdrawn from the after-tax account.                              |
| fm_aTax_bonds   | Bond value withdrawn from the after-tax account.                        |
| fm_aTax_basis   | Cost basis of stocks withdrawn from the after-tax account.              |
| fm_aTax_unrlz   | Unrealised gain or loss on stocks withdrawn from the after-tax account. |
| to_aTax\_\_cash | Cash deposited into the after-tax account.                              |
| to_aTax_bonds   | Bond value deposited into the after-tax account.                        |
| to_aTax_basis   | Cost basis of stock deposited into the after-tax account.               |
| to_aTax_unrlz   | Unrealised gain or loss on stock deposited into the after-tax account.  |

## 1.6 Roth Conversions ($000s)

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                                                         |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| e_RothConv | Amount converted from Person's Tax-Deferred account to their Roth account this year. Counts as taxable ordinary income. |
| j_RothConv | Amount converted from Spouse's Tax-Deferred account to their Roth account this year.                                    |

## 1.7 Income Streams ($000s)

| **Column**     | **Description**                                                                                                                                                   |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| SSA_income     | Social Security Administration (SSA) benefit income for this year. Inflation-adjusted; may be reduced to 77% from 2034 if the SSA reduction scenario is selected. |
| pension_income | Pension or annuity income. May be fixed, COLA-adjusted, or a lump sum received in one year.                                                                       |
| misc_income    | Miscellaneous annual income (e.g. inherited IRA distributions). Grows at the user-specified rate.                                                                 |
| taxfree_income | One-time tax-free income events entered via the 'Phases of Retirement' rows with event type 'One Time Income'.                                                    |
| auto_income    | Sum of all automatic (non-discretionary) income: e_RMD + j_RMD + dividends + misc_income + SSA_income + taxfree_income + pension_income - IRMAA.                  |
| dividends      | Dividend income from the stock portion of the after-tax account.                                                                                                  |

## 1.8 Spending ($000s)

| **Column**    | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| disp_income   | Disposable income (after-tax spending available). This is the variable the optimizer maximises (or holds at a target value when maximising Plan Surplus). In row 0 it holds the user-specified target spending level.                           |
| spend_essence | Essential spending floor for this year. Set via the 'Phases of Retirement' essential spending rows. The optimiser constrains disp_income \>= spend_essence.                                                                                     |
| spend_δ       | Spending growth multiplier for the Changing Consumption spending model (Blanchett formula). In row 0, equals 1 + spending inflation rate. In subsequent rows under the Changing Consumption model, reflects age-adjusted real spending changes. |
| charity       | Annual charitable contribution amount. Used to calculate Qualified Charitable Distributions (QCDs).                                                                                                                                             |

## 1.9 Tax Calculation Columns

Income tax brackets are modelled as a series of 'buckets.' Each bucket
holds the amount of taxable income that falls within a particular
marginal rate band. All values in \$000s.

| **Column**     | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| taxable_income | Total taxable income for the year used to compute income tax. Includes RMDs, discretionary taxd withdrawals, Roth conversions, dividends, 85% of SSA, pension, misc income, less capital losses and QCDs. |
| income_tax     | Total Federal income tax (ordinary income + capital gains tax) for the year.                                                                                                                              |
| tax_bracket    | Marginal income tax rate reached in this year (e.g. 0.22 for 22%). Derived from which tax buckets are non-zero.                                                                                           |
| MAGI           | Modified Adjusted Gross Income for this year. Includes capital gains and the full (not 85%) SSA amount. Used for IRMAA determination.                                                                     |
| tax0           | Width of the 0% ordinary income bracket (standard deduction portion).                                                                                                                                     |
| tax1           | Width of the 10% ordinary income bracket.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| tax2           | Width of the 12% ordinary income bracket.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| tax3           | Width of the 22% ordinary income bracket.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| tax4           | Width of the 24% ordinary income bracket.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| tax5           | Width of the 32% ordinary income bracket.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| tax6           | Width of the 35% ordinary income bracket.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| capgains       | Total realised capital gains from the after-tax account.                                                                                                                                                  |
| caplosss       | Capital losses harvested from the after-tax account (up to \$3,000 per year can offset ordinary income).                                                                                                  |
| cgains_rate    | Marginal capital gains tax rate applied this year (0%, 15%, or 20%).                                                                                                                                      |
| cgt0           | Width of the 0% capital gains tax bracket.                                                                                                                                                                |
| cgt15          | Width of the 15% capital gains tax bracket.                                                                                                                                                               |
| QCD            | Qualified Charitable Distribution amount (reduces taxable RMD income). Available once either spouse reaches age 70.5.                                                                                     |

## 1.10 IRMAA Columns

IRMAA (Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount) is a Medicare premium
surcharge applied to individuals whose MAGI from two years prior exceeds
certain thresholds. All monetary values in \$000s.

| **Column**               | **Description**                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| IRMAA                    | Total Medicare IRMAA surcharge for this year (paid by all eligible people in the household aged 65+).                                                                        |
| IRMAA-bins               | Packed integer encoding of which IRMAA income tiers are reached. Bit 0 (value 1) = tier 0; bit 1 (value 2) = tier 1; etc. A value of 3 means tiers 0 and 1 are both reached. |
| IRMAA-buk0 .. IRMAA-buk5 | Width of each IRMAA income tier bracket (inflation-adjusted). Tier 0 is the base tier; tiers 1–5 are incremental above it.                                                   |
| IRMAA-chg0 .. IRMAA-chg5 | Incremental Medicare surcharge applied per tier per eligible person. Row 0 of IRMAA-buk0 stores the inflation rate (squirrelled metadata — see Section 4).                   |

## 1.11 Asset Allocation & Rate Columns

These columns capture the investment assumptions used in each year of
the plan.

| **Column**   | **Description**                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ror_bonds    | Annual rate of return on the bond portion of all accounts (decimal; e.g. 0.03 = 3%).                                                                             |
| ror_stock    | Annual rate of return on the stock portion of all accounts (decimal). If historical rates are selected, these are replaced by actual historical S&P 500 returns. |
| dvd_stock    | Annual dividend yield on the stock portion of the after-tax account (decimal). Dividends are taxable income.                                                     |
| frac_bonds_a | Fraction of the after-tax account invested in bonds (decimal). May vary by year under the Glide Path option.                                                     |
| frac_stock_a | Fraction of the after-tax account invested in stocks (decimal).                                                                                                  |
| frac_bonds_r | Fraction of Roth accounts invested in bonds (decimal).                                                                                                           |
| frac_stock_r | Fraction of Roth accounts invested in stocks (decimal).                                                                                                          |
| frac_bonds_d | Fraction of Tax-Deferred accounts invested in bonds (decimal).                                                                                                   |
| frac_stock_d | Fraction of Tax-Deferred accounts invested in stocks (decimal).                                                                                                  |

## 1.12 RMD Factor Columns

| **Column**   | **Description**                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| e_RMD_factor | Required Minimum Distribution factor for Person. 0 if age \< 73; otherwise 1 / IRS Uniform Lifetime Table divisor for that age.                      |
| j_RMD_factor | Required Minimum Distribution factor for Spouse. Same logic as e_RMD_factor.                                                                         |
| e_Taxd_in    | Lump sum pension or annuity distribution added to Person's Tax-Deferred account in the year the pension is claimed (non-zero only in that one year). |
| j_Taxd_in    | Lump sum pension distribution added to Spouse's Tax-Deferred account.                                                                                |

## 1.13 OBBBA Column

OBBBA refers to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act retirement bonus
deduction, available through 2028.

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| obbba_pax  | Number of people in the household eligible for the OBBBA \$6,000 bonus standard deduction (persons aged 65 or older, for plan years 2025–2028 only). Value of 0, 1, or 2.                                       |
| QCD_limit  | Maximum Qualified Charitable Distribution allowed this year (per-person limit \* number of persons age 70+, inflation-adjusted). Row 0 of QCD_limit stores MAGI_prebase (squirrelled metadata — see Section 4). |

## 1.14 Summary / Target Columns

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                                                                                                 |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| surplus    | The user-specified Plan Surplus (FTAB) target, inflation-adjusted to each year. Used as the minimum acceptable net_pretax value at the end of the plan horizon. |

# 2. 3-Peat Summary Statistics (sm dictionary)

When running in 3-Peat test mode, after all rolling-horizon projections
are complete a summary dictionary (sm) is displayed. This is not written
to a separate CSV; it is displayed inline. It contains six scalar
values:

| **Field**   | **Description**                                                                                                                           |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| initial_DI  | Disposable income in the first plan year of the final (last) 3-Peat projection run (\$000s).                                              |
| smallest_DI | Minimum disposable income across all plan years across all 3-Peat projections (\$000s). This is a measure of worst-case spending.         |
| mean_DI     | Mean disposable income across all plan years (\$000s).                                                                                    |
| sdtdev_DI   | Standard deviation of disposable income across all plan years (\$000s). Note: field name contains a typo ('sdtdev' rather than 'stddev'). |
| FTAB        | Final Total Account Balance (net_pretax) at the end of the last projection year (\$000s).                                                 |
| sum_DI      | Sum of all disposable income values across all plan years (\$000s). Represents total lifetime spending capacity in the plan.              |

# 3. 3-Peat Rolling Projection CSV Files

In 3-Peat mode, when verbose output is enabled, a separate CSV is
written for each iteration of the rolling projection (one per historical
year simulated). File names are versioned by inserting the iteration
number before the .csv extension (e.g. data/\_explore.1.csv,
data/\_explore.2.csv, ...).

Each file has the same column structure as explore.csv (Section 1), but
values reflect real (inflation-deflated) dollars expressed in base-year
\$000s rather than nominal dollars. Additionally, the rs result-summary
dictionary uses a subset of columns:

| **Column**  | **Description**                                                                                                   |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| year        | Calendar year.                                                                                                    |
| e           | Age of Person.                                                                                                    |
| j           | Age of Spouse.                                                                                                    |
| hist_year   | The historical calendar year whose stock/bond/dividend returns were used as inputs for this projection iteration. |
| ror_stock   | Stock rate of return used (from historical data). Decimal.                                                        |
| dvd_stock   | Dividend yield used (from historical data). Decimal.                                                              |
| ror_bonds   | Bond rate of return used (from historical data). Decimal.                                                         |
| infl_rate   | Spending growth multiplier (spend_δ) for this year.                                                               |
| TAB         | Total Account Balance (net_pretax) at the start of the year (\$000s, real).                                       |
| disp_income | Disposable income (spending) for this year (\$000s, real).                                                        |
| IRMAA       | Medicare IRMAA surcharge (\$000s, real).                                                                          |
| income_tax  | Income tax paid (\$000s, real).                                                                                   |
| deposits    | Deposits into accounts (mapped from SSA_income in the rs dict) (\$000s, real).                                    |
| withdrawals | Withdrawals from accounts (mapped from from_aTax in the rs dict) (\$000s, real).                                  |
| x_RothConv  | Roth conversion amount for Person (e_RothConv) (\$000s, real).                                                    |

# 4. historical/rates.csv (Input File)

This is an input file (not generated by e-ORP) located at
historical/rates.csv. It is loaded at startup and provides historical
annual rates of return used when the user selects a historical year in
the 'Historical Rates' dropdown. The file is indexed by year.

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                               |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| year       | Calendar year (index column). Covers at minimum 1970 to the most recent available year.       |
| S          | Stock (S&P 500 or equivalent) annual rate of return for that year. Decimal (e.g. 0.12 = 12%). |
| B          | Bond (e.g. 10-year US Treasury) annual rate of return. Decimal.                               |
| D          | Stock dividend yield for that year. Decimal.                                                  |

# 5. Row 0 Metadata (Squirrelled Parameters)

Row 0 of the data dictionary is the base year. Several output columns in
row 0 are not meaningful as financial values for that year; instead, the
application stores miscellaneous model configuration parameters in these
cells. This technique is called 'squirrelling'. The mapping from
parameter name to column name is:

| **Parameter Name** | **Stored in Column** | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| inflation          | IRMAA-buk0\[0\]      | Annual inflation rate used for SSA, tax bracket indexing, and spending (decimal, e.g. 0.02 = 2%).                                                                                      |
| filing_status      | tax_bracket\[0\]     | Federal income tax filing status: 0 = Single, 1 = Married Filing Jointly, 2 = Head of Household.                                                                                       |
| MAGI_prebase       | QCD_limit\[0\]       | Modified Adjusted Gross Income from the year prior to the base year (\$000s). Used to determine IRMAA surcharges in year 1.                                                            |
| orp_mode           | IRMAA-buk1\[0\]      | Optimizer mode: 0 = Normal (fastest), 1 = No Capital Losses, 2 = No Basis Averaging, 3 = Neither, 4 = Full MINLP (slowest).                                                            |
| orp_objtv          | IRMAA-buk2\[0\]      | Optimisation objective: 0 = Maximise Spending (disp_income); 'net_pretax' = Maximise Plan Surplus (FTAB).                                                                              |
| eoplan_spouse      | IRMAA-buk3\[0\]      | Year index (relative to base year = 0) at which the spouse leaves the plan (i.e. reaches their planning horizon age). After this year, filing status reverts to Single.                |
| min_realized       | IRMAA-buk4\[0\]      | Minimum Realised Gain setting as a percentage of basis (0–100). Controls floor on capital gains realisation.                                                                           |
| gap_limit          | IRMAA-buk5\[0\]      | Solver gap goal (%). The SCIP solver stops when the optimality gap is at or below this value.                                                                                          |
| scip_status        | IRMAA-chg0\[0\]      | SCIP solver status string after completing the optimisation (e.g. 'optimal', 'timelimit', 'gaplimit', 'infeasible').                                                                   |
| scip_stage         | IRMAA-chg1\[0\]      | SCIP solver stage name at termination.                                                                                                                                                 |
| scip_gap           | IRMAA-chg2\[0\]      | Final optimality gap achieved by the solver (decimal fraction, e.g. 0.001 = 0.1%).                                                                                                     |
| scip_time          | IRMAA-chg3\[0\]      | Total wall-clock time taken by the SCIP solver (seconds).                                                                                                                              |
| time_limit         | IRMAA-chg4\[0\]      | Solver time limit specified by the user (seconds).                                                                                                                                     |
| Roth_conv_max      | IRMAA-chg5\[0\]      | Roth conversion limit setting. Either the string 'unlimited' or the name of the tax bracket variable that must be zero (e.g. 'tax3' means conversions are limited to the 12% bracket). |
| e-ORP_version      | from_aTax\[0\]       | Application version number (numeric).                                                                                                                                                  |

When reading a CSV file programmatically, use the squirrel_map
dictionary in the source code to retrieve these values. For example, to
get the inflation rate: dd\['IRMAA-buk0'\]\[0\].

# 6. 3-Peat Rolling Projection: Relationship to Main Projection Output

This section documents the precise mathematical relationships between
the columns of the 3-Peat rolling-projection CSV files (Section 3) and
the columns of the main projection output CSV (Section 1). Understanding
these relationships is necessary to reconstruct or validate the 3-Peat
summary values from the underlying per-iteration data files.

## 6.1 Overview of the 3-Peat Mechanism

3-Peat runs the optimiser repeatedly, advancing the plan horizon by one
year on each iteration and substituting real historical rates of return
from the historical/rates.csv file. Each iteration i (i = 1, 2, …)
corresponds to one historical calendar year. The per-iteration dd
snapshot written to disk is the full planning data dictionary for that
iteration, in nominal dollars. The rs summary rows written to the final
\_explore.99.csv are derived from iteration i = 1 values of dd, deflated
to real (base-year) dollars.

Key index convention used throughout this section:

| **Symbol**       | **Meaning**                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| i                | Iteration number of the 3-Peat loop (1-based). Corresponds to one historical year.                                                                                                             |
| y                | Plan-year index within a single projection (0 = base year, 1 = first plan year, …).                                                                                                            |
| H_i              | The historical calendar year used for iteration i (stored in rs\[hist_year\]\[i\]).                                                                                                            |
| infl_rate_i      | Historical CPI inflation rate for iteration i, from historical/rates.csv column I (stored in rs\[infl_rate\]\[i\]).                                                                            |
| cumm_infl_i      | Cumulative inflation factor from the original base year to the end of iteration i: product of (1 + infl_rate_k) for k = 1 to i. cumm_infl_0 = 1.                                               |
| dd_i\[col\]\[y\] | Value of column col at plan-year y in the dd dictionary as it exists at the start of iteration i (before the iteration's solver run). This is what gets written to the per-iteration CSV file. |
| rs\[col\]\[i\]   | Value of column col at row i in the 3-Peat summary table (the \_explore.99.csv file).                                                                                                          |

## 6.2 Correction: historical/rates.csv Has a Fourth Column

Section 4 of this document listed three columns (S, B, D) for
historical/rates.csv. The 3-Peat code also reads a fourth column:

| **Column** | **Description**                                                                                                                                |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| I          | Historical annual CPI (or equivalent) inflation rate for that year. Decimal. Used in 3-Peat as infl_rate_i and stored in rs\[infl_rate\]\[i\]. |

## 6.3 Initialisation of rs Before the Loop

Before the first iteration, the rs dictionary is populated by
shallow-copying the initial dd arrays. These values are placeholders
that will be overwritten during the loop; however, row 0 of rs retains
the initial dd values throughout:

```
rs\[year\] = dd\[year\] (list copy)

rs\[e\] = dd\[e\] (list copy)

rs\[j\] = dd\[j\] (list copy)

rs\[hist_year\] = dd\[year\] (list copy; overwritten per-iteration for
rows 1..N)

rs\[ror_stock\] = dd\[ror_stock\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration for
rows 1..N)

rs\[dvd_stock\] = dd\[dvd_stock\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration for
rows 1..N)

rs\[ror_bonds\] = dd\[ror_bonds\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration for
rows 1..N)

rs\[infl_rate\] = dd\[spend_delta\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration
for rows 1..N)

rs\[TAB\] = dd\[net_pretax\] (copy; row 1 then overwritten — see §6.4)

rs\[disp_income\] = dd\[disp_income\] (copy; overwritten
per-iteration)

rs\[IRMAA\] = dd\[IRMAA\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration)

rs\[income_tax\] = dd\[income_tax\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration)

rs\[deposits\] = dd\[SSA_income\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration —
see §6.6)

rs\[withdrawals\] = dd\[from_aTax\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration —
see §6.6)

rs\[x_RothConv\] = dd\[e_RothConv\] (copy; overwritten per-iteration —
see §6.6)
```

Additionally, rs\[TAB\]\[1\] is set once before the loop to the sum of
initial account balances (nominal \$000s):

```
rs\[TAB\]\[1\] = dd\[afterTax\]\[0\] + dd\[e_Taxd\]\[0\] +
dd\[j_Taxd\]\[0\]

\+ dd\[e_Roth\]\[0\] + dd\[j_Roth\]\[0\]
```

This represents the total portfolio value at the very start of the plan
(before any year-1 transactions), in nominal dollars. It is later
overwritten at the end of each iteration (see §6.5).

## 6.4 Per-Iteration CSV File (dd_i snapshot)

At the start of each iteration i, after the solver runs but before
historical rates are applied, the current state of dd is written to disk
as data/\_explore.{i}.csv. Because the write occurs before the
historical-rate override, all account-balance columns in this file
reflect the values computed by the solver using its assumed return rates
(dd\[ror_stock\]\[y\] and dd\[ror_bonds\]\[y\]), not the historical
rates from historical/rates.csv.

The following identities hold for y = 1 in the per-iteration CSV, using
the assumed return rates stored in the file itself:

Assumed return factors (y = 1 values in the per-iteration CSV)

```
a_rori_r(1) = 1 + dd\[ror_stock\]\[1\] \* frac_stock_r\[1\] +
dd\[ror_bonds\]\[1\] \* frac_bonds_r\[1\]

a_rori_d(1) = 1 + dd\[ror_stock\]\[1\] \* frac_stock_d\[1\] +
dd\[ror_bonds\]\[1\] \* frac_bonds_d\[1\]
```

where dd\[ror_stock\]\[1\] and dd\[ror_bonds\]\[1\] are the assumed
return rates used by the solver for plan year 1 (read from the
per-iteration CSV file). These are the rates the solver used when
optimising; they are not the historical rates from historical/rates.csv.

Assumed-rate account balance identities (y = 1 in the per-iteration CSV)

The following identities relate the y = 1 account balances in the
per-iteration CSV to the y = 0 base-year values, using the assumed
return factors defined above:

```
dd\[e_Taxd\]\[1\] = a_rori_d(1) \* (dd\[e_Taxd\]\[0\] -
dd\[e_RMD\]\[1\] - dd\[e_RothConv\]\[1\]

\- dd\[from_eTaxd\]\[1\] + dd\[e_Taxd_in\]\[1\])

dd\[j_Taxd\]\[1\] = a_rori_d(1) \* (dd\[j_Taxd\]\[0\] -
dd\[j_RMD\]\[1\] - dd\[j_RothConv\]\[1\]

\- dd\[from_jTaxd\]\[1\] + dd\[j_Taxd_in\]\[1\])

dd\[e_Roth\]\[1\] = a_rori_r(1) \* (dd\[e_Roth\]\[0\] -
dd\[from_eRoth\]\[1\] + dd\[e_RothConv\]\[1\])

dd\[j_Roth\]\[1\] = a_rori_r(1) \* (dd\[j_Roth\]\[0\] -
dd\[from_jRoth\]\[1\] + dd\[j_RothConv\]\[1\])
```

The solver uses dd\[ror_stock\]\[y\] and dd\[ror_bonds\]\[y\] as return
rates for all plan years y = 1..N, so analogous identities hold for y =
2..N in the CSV using the corresponding frac\_\* values for each year.

Dividend adjustment for year 1

Because the historical dividend rate dvd_stock_i may differ from the
assumed dividend rate used by the solver in year 1, a cash adjustment is
applied after the solver runs:

```
assumed_div = dd\[dividends\]\[1\]

actual_divd = ror_bonds_i \* dd\[aTax_bonds\]\[0\]

\+ dvd_stock_i \* (dd\[aTax_basis\]\[0\] + dd\[aTax_unrlz\]\[0\])
```

If actual_divd \< assumed_div (dividends were over-estimated by the
solver):

```
if dd\[aTax\_\_cash\]\[1\] \> (assumed_div - actual_divd):

dd\[aTax\_\_cash\]\[1\] -= (assumed_div - actual_divd)

dd\[afterTax\]\[1\] -= (assumed_div - actual_divd)

else:

dd\[disp_income\]\[1\] -= (assumed_div - actual_divd)
```

If actual_divd \>= assumed_div (dividends were under-estimated):

```
dd\[aTax\_\_cash\]\[1\] -= (assumed_div - actual_divd) \[subtracting a
negative = adding\]

dd\[afterTax\]\[1\] -= (assumed_div - actual_divd)
```

Historical-rate override for the next iteration’s base year

After writing the per-iteration CSV and after the dividend adjustment,
3-Peat recomputes the y = 1 TaxD and Roth account balances using the
actual historical rates for iteration i (columns S and B of
historical/rates.csv). These overwritten values are NOT reflected in the
CSV file; they become the base-year (y = 0) inputs for the next
iteration after dd is advanced (see §6.6).

Historical return factors

```
n_rori_r(1) = 1 + ror_stock_i \* frac_stock_r\[1\] + ror_bonds_i \*
frac_bonds_r\[1\]

n_rori_d(1) = 1 + ror_stock_i \* frac_stock_d\[1\] + ror_bonds_i \*
frac_bonds_d\[1\]
```

where ror_stock_i = row\['S'\] and ror_bonds_i = row\['B'\] from
historical/rates.csv for iteration i.

The overwritten account balances are:

```
dd\[e_Taxd\]\[1\] ← n_rori_d(1) \* (dd\[e_Taxd\]\[0\] -
dd\[e_RMD\]\[1\] - dd\[e_RothConv\]\[1\]

\- dd\[from_eTaxd\]\[1\] + dd\[e_Taxd_in\]\[1\])

dd\[j_Taxd\]\[1\] ← n_rori_d(1) \* (dd\[j_Taxd\]\[0\] -
dd\[j_RMD\]\[1\] - dd\[j_RothConv\]\[1\]

\- dd\[from_jTaxd\]\[1\] + dd\[j_Taxd_in\]\[1\])

dd\[e_Roth\]\[1\] ← n_rori_r(1) \* (dd\[e_Roth\]\[0\] -
dd\[from_eRoth\]\[1\] + dd\[e_RothConv\]\[1\])

dd\[j_Roth\]\[1\] ← n_rori_r(1) \* (dd\[j_Roth\]\[0\] -
dd\[from_jRoth\]\[1\] + dd\[j_RothConv\]\[1\])
```

Note: afterTax\[1\] is not overridden here; only TaxD and Roth accounts
are adjusted by 3-Peat using historical rates. The afterTax balance
carries the assumed-rate solver value into the dividend adjustment step
that follows.

## 6.5 rs Summary Row i: Derivation from dd Year-1 Values

After the historical-rate override and dividend adjustment for iteration
i, the summary row rs\[\*\]\[i\] is computed by deflating nominal dd
year-1 values by cumm_infl_i. Important: rs\[disp_income\]\[i\] uses the
post-dividend-adjustment value of dd\[disp_income\]\[1\] (which may
differ from the CSV value if the cash-drain branch was taken — see §6.4
Dividend adjustment). Similarly, rs\[TAB\]\[i+1\] is computed from the
historically-adjusted account balances, not from the CSV values.

```
cumm_infl_i = cumm_infl\_{i-1} \* (1 + infl_rate_i)

= product\_{k=1}^{i} (1 + infl_rate_k)
```

where infl_rate_i = row\['I'\] from historical/rates.csv for the year
H_i.

Rate columns (no deflation — these are already rates/factors)

```
rs\[hist_year\]\[i\] = H_i (the historical calendar year)

rs\[ror_stock\]\[i\] = row\['S'\] for year H_i

rs\[ror_bonds\]\[i\] = row\['B'\] for year H_i

rs\[dvd_stock\]\[i\] = row\['D'\] for year H_i

rs\[infl_rate\]\[i\] = row\['I'\] for year H_i
```

Deflated flow columns (nominal dd values / cumm_infl_i)

```
rs\[disp_income\]\[i\] = dd\[disp_income\]\[1\] / cumm_infl_i

rs\[income_tax\]\[i\] = dd\[income_tax\]\[1\] / cumm_infl_i

rs\[IRMAA\]\[i\] = dd\[IRMAA\]\[1\] / cumm_infl_i

rs\[x_RothConv\]\[i\] = (dd\[e_RothConv\]\[1\] +
dd\[j_RothConv\]\[1\]) / cumm_infl_i
```

rs\[deposits\]\[i\] — composite income deflated

Despite its name (initialised from dd\[SSA_income\]),
rs\[deposits\]\[i\] is a composite that includes all non-discretionary
income sources flowing into year 1:

```
rs\[deposits\]\[i\] = ( dd\[SSA_income\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[misc_income\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[pension_income\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[taxfree_income\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[dividends\]\[1\] ) / cumm_infl_i
```

rs\[withdrawals\]\[i\] — composite account withdrawals deflated

Despite its name (initialised from dd\[from_aTax\]),
rs\[withdrawals\]\[i\] is a composite of all discretionary and mandatory
withdrawals from all accounts (net of any deposit back into the
after-tax account):

```
rs\[withdrawals\]\[i\] = ( dd\[e_RMD\]\[1\] + dd\[j_RMD\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[from_eTaxd\]\[1\] + dd\[from_jTaxd\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[from_aTax\]\[1\] - dd\[to_aTax\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[from_eRoth\]\[1\] + dd\[from_jRoth\]\[1\] ) / cumm_infl_i
```

rs\[TAB\]\[i+1\] — end-of-year-1 total account balance, deflated
(historically adjusted)

rs\[TAB\]\[i+1\] represents the total portfolio value at the end of plan
year 1 of iteration i (equivalently, the base-year starting value for
iteration i+1), deflated to real \$000s. It is computed from the
historically-adjusted account balances — i.e. the values after the
historical-rate override and dividend adjustment, not the assumed-rate
values in the per-iteration CSV:

```
rs\[TAB\]\[i+1\] = ( dd\[afterTax\]\[1\] + dd\[e_Taxd\]\[1\] +
dd\[j_Taxd\]\[1\]

\+ dd\[e_Roth\]\[1\] + dd\[j_Roth\]\[1\] ) / cumm_infl_i
```

Note: rs\[TAB\]\[1\] is set before the loop (see §6.3) and is not
subject to deflation; it is a nominal value.

## 6.6 Advancing dd Between Iterations

At the end of each iteration, dd is modified to prepare for the next
iteration. Three transformations are applied in order:

Step 1: Propagate squirrelled metadata from row 0 to row 1

For every column that stores squirrelled metadata in row 0 (see Section
5), the row-0 value is copied into row 1 before the row-0 slice is
dropped:

```
for each column c in squirrel_map.values():

dd\[c\]\[1\] = dd\[c\]\[0\]
```

Step 2: Adjust inflation-sensitive bracket and SSA values for rows 2..N

When the historical inflation rate infl_rate_i differs from the model
inflation rate (get_nut(dd,'inflation') = infl), the difference must be
applied to the remaining years' bracket widths and SSA income. An
adjustment factor is computed:

```
infl_adj = 1 + (infl_rate_i - infl)
```

This factor is then applied multiplicatively to the following columns
for all y in 2..N:

| **Columns adjusted by infl_adj**         |
|------------------------------------------|
| QCD_limit, IRMAA-buk0 .. IRMAA-buk5      |
| IRMAA-chg0 .. IRMAA-chg5                 |
| tax0, tax1, tax2, tax3, tax4, tax5, tax6 |
| cgt0, cgt15                              |
| SSA_income                               |
| surplus                                  |

Step 3: Drop the base year (row 0) and shift the horizon back by one

The entire dd dictionary is trimmed by removing index 0, so that the
next iteration's year-0 is the current year-1:

```
dd\[c\] = dd\[c\]\[1:\] for all columns c
```

The eoplan_spouse squirrelled parameter is then decremented by 1 to
maintain its meaning as a relative offset:

```
eoplan_spouse = eoplan_spouse - 1
```

## 6.7 Summary Statistics (sm dictionary)

After the loop over all N iterations completes, the sm summary
statistics are computed from the rs array. Let i_max be the index of the
last completed iteration:

```
sm\[initial_DI\] = rs\[disp_income\]\[1\]

sm\[smallest_DI\] = min(rs\[disp_income\]\[1\],
rs\[disp_income\]\[2\], ..., rs\[disp_income\]\[i_max\])

sm\[mean_DI\] = mean(rs\[disp_income\]\[1..i_max\])

sm\[sdtdev_DI\] = sample_stdev(rs\[disp_income\]\[1..i_max\])

sm\[FTAB\] = rs\[TAB\]\[i_max + 1\]

sm\[sum_DI\] = sum(rs\[disp_income\]\[1..i_max\])
```

All sm values are in real (base-year) \$000s, consistent with the rs
deflation applied in §6.5.

## 6.8 Worked Example: Reconstructing rs[i] Flow Columns From a
Per-Iteration CSV

Given the per-iteration file \_explore.i.csv and knowledge of
cumm_infl_i, the flow summary columns can be reconstructed as follows.
Note that rs\[TAB\]\[i+1\] cannot be reconstructed from the
per-iteration CSV alone because it is computed from the
historically-adjusted account balances (after the CSV write); see §6.4
and §6.5.

```
// All values read from \_explore.i.csv, row y=1

rs\[disp_income\]\[i\] = file\[disp_income\]\[1\] / cumm_infl_i

rs\[income_tax\]\[i\] = file\[income_tax\]\[1\] / cumm_infl_i

rs\[IRMAA\]\[i\] = file\[IRMAA\]\[1\] / cumm_infl_i

rs\[x_RothConv\]\[i\] = (file\[e_RothConv\]\[1\] +
file\[j_RothConv\]\[1\]) / cumm_infl_i

rs\[deposits\]\[i\] = (file\[SSA_income\]\[1\] +
file\[misc_income\]\[1\]

\+ file\[pension_income\]\[1\] + file\[taxfree_income\]\[1\]

\+ file\[dividends\]\[1\]) / cumm_infl_i

rs\[withdrawals\]\[i\] = (file\[e_RMD\]\[1\] + file\[j_RMD\]\[1\]

\+ file\[from_eTaxd\]\[1\] + file\[from_jTaxd\]\[1\]

\+ file\[from_aTax\]\[1\] - file\[to_aTax\]\[1\]

\+ file\[from_eRoth\]\[1\] + file\[from_jRoth\]\[1\]) / cumm_infl_i

// rs\[TAB\]\[i+1\] cannot be read directly from the per-iteration
CSV.

// See §6.4 (Historical-rate override) and §6.5 (rs\[TAB\]\[i+1\]) for
the correct derivation.
```

To compute cumm_infl_i iteratively: start with cumm_infl_0 = 1.0, then
for each iteration k = 1 to i, multiply by (1 + rs\[infl_rate\]\[k\]),
where rs\[infl_rate\]\[k\] is the value stored in the final
\_explore.99.csv.

## 6.9 Distinction Between infl_rate and the Model Inflation Rate

Two different inflation concepts appear in the 3-Peat files:

| **Parameter**                                    | **Source**                                 | **Role**                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| infl_rate (rs\[infl_rate\]\[i\])                 | historical/rates.csv column I for year H_i | Actual historical CPI for that year. Used to compute cumm_infl_i and to adjust tax brackets/SSA in subsequent iterations via infl_adj.                                                                |
| inflation (squirrelled in dd\[IRMAA-buk0\]\[0\]) | User input (Inflation % widget)            | Model inflation assumption used to project SSA, tax brackets, and spending targets within a single projection run. Constant across all plan years within an iteration.                                |
| infl_adj                                         | Derived: 1 + (infl_rate_i - inflation)     | Multiplicative correction applied to brackets and SSA for years 2..N at the end of each iteration to reconcile the difference between what actually happened (historical) and what the model assumed. |
